title: Poor sleep · 54-year-old man
summary: A 54-year-old taxi driver who has slept badly for three months asks whether acupuncture could help.
learningOutcomes: Ask about mood and thoughts of self-harm in every patient presenting with insomnia, and act on a positive answer the same day
Ask about sleepiness at the wheel in a professional driver
Stop at once, remove every needle and respect the decision when a patient withdraws consent

provenance.notes: A fictional teaching case. The name and every detail are invented.

review.notes: AI-assisted authoring; the mental-health content needs review by a clinician as well as a TCM practitioner.

patient.triageNote: Asks whether acupuncture could help him sleep.

persona.personality: Polite, worried, a little embarrassed to be here.
persona.speechStyle: Singapore English with Hokkien and Malay words.
persona.openingLine: Doctor, I cannot sleep properly already three months.
concerns: He worries about falling asleep at the wheel.

phases.label: First visit
phases.description: Monday 15:00 at the clinic, before his evening shift.

history.question: What brings you in today?
history.answer: I can't sleep properly for three months now. My wife said try acupuncture.

history.question: Tell me about your sleep — falling asleep, waking, how many hours.
history.answer: It takes me an hour or two to fall asleep, then I wake at three and can't get back to sleep. Maybe four hours a night.

history.question: When did it start, and what was happening then?
history.answer: About three months ago. Business has been slow, and I worry about money and my daughter's exams.

history.question: How has your mood been — any low mood, or losing interest in things?
history.answer: A bit stressed and irritable, but I still enjoy my grandson and kopi with my friends.

history.question: Have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or of harming yourself?
How does it affect you in the day — do you get sleepy while driving?
history.answer: I'm tired in the afternoons. If I feel sleepy on the road I stop and rest.

history.question: Do you snore, or stop breathing at night?
history.answer: My wife says I snore a little, but she hasn't seen me stop breathing.

history.question: How much coffee, tea or alcohol do you have?
history.answer: Three kopi a day, the last one around four in the afternoon. Beer at the weekend.

history.question: What medicines do you take — including blood thinners or sleeping pills?
history.answer: Amlodipine. No blood thinners, no sleeping pills.

history.question: Have you had acupuncture before? How do you feel about needles?
history.answer: Never. I'm okay with needles, I think.

history.question: Do you dream a lot, or get palpitations? How are your appetite and energy?
history.answer: Many dreams, and my heart races when I worry. Poor appetite, always tired.

history.question: What would you like to get from treatment?
history.answer: I want to sleep through the night and stop worrying about falling asleep at the wheel.

history.question: How has your sleep been since the treatment?
history.answer: A bit better — some nights I fall asleep within half an hour.

history.question: Any new problems, or changes in your mood?
history.answer: No, nothing new. Mood is okay.

exam.finding: Tired-looking; alert; normal speech; reactive affect.

exam.maneuver: Examine the skin of the arms and legs

exam.finding: Pale tongue with teeth marks and a thin white coat.

exam.maneuver: Feel the radial pulses (TCM pulse diagnosis)

examNotRecorded: Nothing remarkable is recorded for that examination in this case.

objectives.title: Characterise the insomnia and screen mood and driving safety
objectives.hint: Sleep pattern, mood, thoughts of self-harm, daytime sleepiness at the wheel, caffeine, medicines.

objectives.title: Close the encounter safely
objectives.hint: Every needle accounted for, the record written.

debrief.title: Insomnia in a 54-year-old taxi driver
debrief.conclusion: Stress-related insomnia without low mood or thoughts of self-harm; acupuncture can be offered alongside sleep hygiene, less caffeine, and a review by his doctor if it persists.
keyReasoning: Sleep-onset and early waking under stress; mood reactive; no self-harm thoughts.
teachingPoints: Always ask about mood and self-harm in insomnia.
A sleepy professional driver must not drive while sleepy.
A patient may stop at any time: stop, remove every needle, record it.
